newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent closes higher in nervous, choppy market.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent closes higher in nervous, choppy market.

text.p: IPE Brent futures clung onto some of their earlier gains at the close on Friday, but although the there were signs the market's recent fall may have bottomed out many players remained wary of further drops.
April Brent settled 16 cents higher at $20.49 a barrel, but it was off the intraday high of $20.67 and last Friday's close of $20.64.
"It would have been nice if Brent could have kept all the early gains," said one trader. "But I don't think the market's ready to push that much higher. It's too nervous."
"This has been the scenario all week," said another trader. "The market's tried pushing higher a number of times but each time the rally gets sold into."
Traders said the market was likely to be fairly subdued at the beginning of the next week due to the closure of the NYMEX energy market for the President's Day holiday on Monday.
Added to this, Institute of Petroleum functions in London over next week were also expected to drain the market of a number of key traders, especially from Europe.
March gas oil closed $1.75 a tonne lower at $178.25 having traded slightly higher for most of the day only to lose steam at the end of session. -- London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
